author: Sherlock, separate read-only design session; not an external human author
randomization: Sort repetition IDs 1,2,3 by SHA-256(seed + ':pair:' + repetition). First pair's first arm is Wisp if the first byte of SHA-256(seed + ':first-arm') is even, otherwise TypeScript. Alternate first arm across pairs. Each pair contains both arms for that repetition. Fixed before attempts.
time_limit_enforcement: Instructional target, not a technical agent timeout. Subprocess commands have independent operational caps.
change_rule: One or two existing parsed function bodies only. All other bytes, sample_* functions, probes, public tests, signatures, record/type declarations and historical material remain unchanged.
task_scope: One synthetic single-file dependency workspace per arm, 15 functions and 3 record types. Not a production repository, module experiment, or six independent tasks.
isolation: Fresh sessions and instruction-only restricted input lists in assigned checkout, not a technical holdout sandbox.
feedback: Self-authored tests allowed; no parent solution coaching, sibling feedback or grader feedback before all six finals are locked.
metrics: Functional acceptance and structured history assertions scored separately. Host dispatch-window elapsed time is not model latency. Backend counts/bytes/time are not comparative agent cost. No token-cost or causal-superiority claim.
capability_interpretation: This task deliberately fits current language features. Failure to support a broader useful workflow is a capability gap, not automatically an architectural disadvantage; this task cannot settle that broader question.
